# CMatrix

Matrix-like effect in your terminal

## Overview

CMatrix is based on the screensaver from The Matrix website. It shows text
flying in and out in a terminal like as seen in "The Matrix" movie. It can
scroll lines all at the same rate or asynchronously and at a user-defined
speed.

CMatrix is inspired from 'The Matrix' movie.

> Disclaimer: We are in no way affiliated with the movie "The Matrix", "Warner Bros" nor
any of its affiliates in any way, just fans.

## Usage

Run CMatrix with the following command:
```sh
cmatrix
```

Run with different arguments to get different effects:
```sh
cmatrix [-abBflohnsmVx] [-u update] [-C color]
```

Example:
```sh
cmatrix -ba -u 2 -C red
```

### Command-line Options

- `-a` - Asynchronous scroll
- `-b` - Bold characters on
- `-B` - All bold characters (overrides -b)
- `-f` - Force the linux $TERM type to be on
- `-l` - Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
- `-o` - Use old-style scrolling
- `-c` - Only print the shadows of letters
- `-L` - Locks cmatrix, unable to quit
- `-h, -?` - Print usage and exit
- `-r` - "Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored characters
- `-k` - Every characters change
- `-n` - No bold characters (overrides -b and -B)
- `-s` - "Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
- `-m` - "Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
- `-x` - X window mode
- `-V` - Print version information and exit
- `-u delay` - Screen update delay 0-9, default 4
- `-C color` - Use this color for matrix (default green). Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
- `-M message` - Add a message in the center of cmatrix
- `-t tty` - Set tty to use

### Interactive Keystrokes

The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in -s mode):

- `a` - Toggle asynchronous scroll
- `b` - Random bold characters
- `B` - All bold characters
- `n` - Turn off bold characters
- `0-9` - Adjust update speed
- `! @ # $ % ^ & )` - Change the color of the matrix:
  - `!` - red
  - `@` - green
  - `#` - yellow
  - `$` - blue
  - `%` - magenta
  - `^` - cyan
  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

## Screenshots

![cmatrix screenshot](./data/img/capture_bold_font.png)

## Screencasts

![cmatrix screencast](./data/img/capture_orig.gif)

## License

This software is provided under the GNU GPL v3. [View License](./COPYING)

  - `&` - white
  - `)` - black
- `q` - Quit the program

### Tips

- To get the program to look most like the movie, use: `cmatrix -lba`
- To get the program to look most like the Win/Mac screensaver, use: `cmatrix -ol`

Note: cmatrix is probably not particularly portable or efficient, but it won't hog
too much CPU time.

.TH CMatrix 1 "Mon May 3 1999"
.SH NAME
CMatrix
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B cmatrix
[\-abBflohnsmVx] [\-u update] [\-C color]
.SH DESCRIPTION
Shows a scrolling 'Matrix' like screen in Linux
.SS OPTIONS
.TP
.I "\-a"
Asynchronous scroll
.TP
.I "\-b"
Bold characters on
.TP
.I "\-B"
All bold characters (overrides \-b)
.TP
.I "\-f"
Force the linux $TERM type to be on
.TP
.I "\-l"
Linux mode (sets "matrix.fnt" font in console)
.TP
.I "\-o"
Use old-style scrolling
.TP
.I "\-c"
Only print the shadows of letters 
.TP
.I "\-L"
Locks cmatrix, Unable to quit
.TP
.I "\-h, \-?"
Print usage and exit
.TP
.I "\-r"
"Rainbow" mode, rainbow colored character
.TP
.I "\-k"
Every characters change 
.TP
.I "\-n"
No bold characters (overrides \-b and \-B)
.TP
.I "\-s"
"Screensaver" mode, exits on first keystroke
.TP
.I "\-m"
"Lambda" mode, every character becomes a lambda
.TP
.I "\-x"
X window mode, use if your xterm is using mtx.pcf
.TP
.I "\-V"
Print version information and exit
.TP
.I "\-u delay"
Screen update delay 0 - 9, default 4
.TP
.I "\-C color"
Use this color for matrix (default green).
Valid colors are green, red, blue, white, yellow, cyan, magenta and black.
.TP
.I "\-M message"
Add a message in the center of cmatrix
.TP
.I "\-t tty"
Set tty to use
.SS KEYSTROKES
The following keystrokes are available during execution (unavailable in
\-s mode)
.TP
.I "a"
Toggle asynchronous scroll
.TP
.I "b"
Random bold characters
.TP
.I "B"
All bold characters
.TP
.I "n"
Turn off bold characters
.TP
.I "0\-9"
Adjust update speed
.TP
.I "! @ # $ % ^ & )"
Change the color of the matrix to the corresponding color:
! \- red, @ \- green, # \- yellow, $ \- blue, % \- magenta, ^ \- cyan,
& \- white, ) \- black.
.TP
.I "q"
Quit the program
.SH BUGS
This program is very CPU intensive.  Don't be surprised if it eats up over
40% of your CPU at times.
.SH HOMEPAGE
http://www.github.com/abishekvashok/cmatrix

#!/bin/sh
# Builds cmatrix-like executable.
set -e
SRC_DIR="$(dirname "$0")"
cd "$SRC_DIR"
CC="${CC:-gcc}"
CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}"
# Link against ncursesw + tinfo. We intentionally do not require the
# ncurses development headers because they are often unavailable; we
# supply a minimal subset of the curses declarations ourselves.
$CC $CFLAGS -o executable src/cmatrix.c -l:libncursesw.so.6 -l:libtinfo.so.6
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
cat compile.sh

cat > compile.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Build script for the cmatrix reimplementation.
set -e

SRC_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$SRC_DIR"

CC="${CC:-gcc}"
CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}"

# Locate ncursesw runtime shared library. We deliberately avoid the
# ncurses development headers because they are frequently absent; a
# minimal subset of declarations is included in src/curses_decls.h.
find_lib() {
    name="$1"
    for dir in /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu /usr/lib \
               /lib /usr/local/lib; do
        if [ -e "$dir/lib${name}.so.6" ]; then
            echo "$dir/lib${name}.so.6"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    # Fall back to ld resolving -lname
    echo "-l${name}"
}

NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncursesw)"
TINFO_LIB="$(find_lib tinfo)"

${CC} ${CFLAGS} -o executable src/cmatrix.c "${NCURSES_LIB}" "${TINFO_LIB}"
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
./compile.sh 2>&1
ls -la executable
./executable -V

cat > compile.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Build script for the cmatrix reimplementation.
set -e

SRC_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$SRC_DIR"

CC="${CC:-gcc}"
CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}"

# Locate an ncurses runtime shared library.  We intentionally do not
# require ncurses development headers; a minimal subset of declarations
# is supplied in src/curses_decls.h.
find_lib() {
    name="$1"
    for dir in /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
               /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu \
               /usr/lib64 /usr/lib /lib /usr/local/lib; do
        for ext in .so.6 .so.5 .so; do
            if [ -e "$dir/lib${name}${ext}" ]; then
                echo "$dir/lib${name}${ext}"
                return 0
            fi
        done
    done
    # Fallback: let the linker resolve -lname
    echo "-l${name}"
}

NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncursesw)"
case "$NCURSES_LIB" in
    -l*)
        # Wide-character ncurses missing, fall back to libncurses
        NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncurses)"
        ;;
esac
TINFO_LIB="$(find_lib tinfo)"

echo "using ncurses: $NCURSES_LIB"
echo "using tinfo:   $TINFO_LIB"

${CC} ${CFLAGS} -o executable src/cmatrix.c "${NCURSES_LIB}" "${TINFO_LIB}"
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh
./compile.sh 2>&1

#!/bin/sh
# Build script for the cmatrix reimplementation.
set -e

SRC_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$SRC_DIR"

CC="${CC:-gcc}"
CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}"

# Locate an ncurses runtime shared library.  We intentionally do not
# require ncurses development headers; a minimal subset of declarations
# is supplied in src/curses_decls.h.
find_lib() {
    name="$1"
    for dir in /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu \
               /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu \
               /usr/lib64 /usr/lib /lib /usr/local/lib; do
        for ext in .so.6 .so.5 .so; do
            if [ -e "$dir/lib${name}${ext}" ]; then
                echo "$dir/lib${name}${ext}"
                return 0
            fi
        done
    done
    # Fallback: let the linker resolve -lname
    echo "-l${name}"
}

NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncursesw)"
case "$NCURSES_LIB" in
    -l*)
        # Wide-character ncurses missing, fall back to libncurses
        NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncurses)"
        ;;
esac
TINFO_LIB="$(find_lib tinfo)"

echo "using ncurses: $NCURSES_LIB"
echo "using tinfo:   $TINFO_LIB"

${CC} ${CFLAGS} -o executable src/cmatrix.c "${NCURSES_LIB}" "${TINFO_LIB}"
---
executable
executable.new
*.o
*.out
build/
</output>

               /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu \
               /usr/lib64 /usr/lib /lib /usr/local/lib; do
        for ext in .so.6 .so.5 .so; do
            if [ -e "$dir/lib${name}${ext}" ]; then
                echo "$dir/lib${name}${ext}"
                return 0
            fi
        done
    done
    # Fallback: let the linker resolve -lname
    echo "-l${name}"
}

NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncursesw)"
case "$NCURSES_LIB" in
    -l*)
        # Wide-character ncurses missing, fall back to libncurses
        NCURSES_LIB="$(find_lib ncurses)"
        ;;
esac
TINFO_LIB="$(find_lib tinfo)"

echo "using ncurses: $NCURSES_LIB"
echo "using tinfo:   $TINFO_LIB"

${CC} ${CFLAGS} -o executable src/cmatrix.c "${NCURSES_LIB}" "${TINFO_LIB}"
---
executable
executable.new
*.o
*.out
build/
</output>

cat > HACKING.md <<'EOF'
# Development notes

This directory contains a reimplementation of the `cmatrix` tool.

## Building

```sh
./compile.sh
```

This will produce a binary called `executable` in the workspace root.
Because the ncurses development headers are frequently absent on
minimal Linux systems, `compile.sh` does not rely on them; a small
subset of the declarations that cmatrix actually uses is kept in
`src/curses_decls.h`, and the shared library `libncursesw.so.6`
(falling back to `libncurses.so.6`) is located at build time and
linked in explicitly.

## Source files

* `src/cmatrix.c` — main program: argument parsing, animation loop,
  signal handling.
* `src/curses_decls.h` — minimal replacement for `<ncurses.h>`.

## Testing

The reference binary is not needed at runtime; `./executable` is built
from source every time.  Basic command-line tests include:

```
./executable -V              # print version info
./executable -h              # print usage
./executable -C purple       # error: invalid color (exit 1)
./executable -t /nosuchfile  # error: couldn't open (exit 1)
./executable -l              # error when setfont/consolechars missing
```
EOF
git add -A
git commit -m "Add HACKING notes"
